decision.title: Budgets follow features; do not block on the owner (owner)
decision.summary: The full and CLI module budgets rise as features land, the core stays lean, reversible open questions take the proposed default, and only the license, releases and npm name wait for the owner.

body.p: on the owner's word: "don't block on me, you can keep raising the budget -- this is for people who want a full blown sxml processor but not hundreds of megabytes to get java".

item.p: The size budgets of the full module and the CLI module rise as features land; a packet that goes over raises the budget in the same change, says so in its commit message and its D-record, and measures the cost. The core sxml.wasm should stay lean: large features go behind 's optional features, and the core budget rises only for small, general additions.

Open questions that are not irreversible take the proposed default and are recorded, so work never waits: 's Phase 7 gate numbers; adding the iXML tests and a sample of Unicode's CollationTest as vendored test data (); the languages en, de, fr, it, es, nl, the calendars ISO, AD, BE, JE, OS, AH and CLDR's standard tailorings for those languages; the XPath 4.0 §3.4.1 reading of number conversion in compatibility mode (); a processor option for the XML version of query text (), defaulting to 1.0.
Still left to the owner, because they are outward-facing or legal: the license, tagging and publishing releases, and the npm package name.
